name: Rivastigmine
mechanism: Reversible cholinesterase inhibitor (both acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase)
dosing: Oral: start 1.5mg BD, increase gradually to 3-6mg BD. Transdermal patch: 4.6mg/24h initially
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to rivastigmine or excipients; caution in patients with cardiac conduction abnormalities or severe hepatic impairment
interactions: Cholinergic and anticholinergic drugs may antagonise effects; caution with other cholinesterase inhibitors; review concomitant medications that increase cholinergic burden
monitoring: Monitor for gastrointestinal adverse effects, weight loss and signs of bradycardia or syncope; assess cognitive and functional response regularly; patch application sites should be inspected for local skin reactions
pregnancy: Avoid unless benefits justify potential risks; limited data available
sideEffects: Gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea), anorexia and weight loss, dizziness and headache; transdermal patch may cause local skin reactions
pharmacokinetics: Available orally and as a transdermal patch; relatively short systemic half-life with prolonged central cholinesterase inhibition
clinicalPearls: Transdermal formulation typically better tolerated gastrointestinally and may improve adherence; useful in Parkinson's disease dementia as well as Alzheimer’s disease
indication: Mild to moderate Alzheimer’s disease and cognitive symptoms in Parkinson’s disease dementia
